result.reason: The operative language gives Company a 30-day written convenience-termination right and a refund of prepaid fees attributable to the post-termination period, while limiting Contractor’s right to periods when no Statement of Work remains outstanding and requiring 90 days’ notice. This substantively reaches the preferred position for Company and the fallback protection against Contractor termination during a committed SOW. It is not strictly minimal because allowing Company to terminate any SOW “in whole or in part” adds a partial-scope termination right beyond the stated playbook requirement. Drafting is otherwise professional, though “pro-rata” could be stated expressly and Contractor’s notice should also be specified as written.
